title.narrative: UNECA 2023 Conference on Land Policy in Africa (AUC, AfDB, UNECA-LPC)
UNECA 2023 Conference on Land Policy in Africa (AUC, AfDB, UNECA-LPC)

description.narrative:
Overall Objective
The overall objective of the Conference is to deepen commitment and strengthen capacity for land policy development, implementation and monitoring in Africa through improved access to knowledge and information in support of evidence based land policy making.
The specific objectives of the Conference are to:
i. Share and exchange knowledge and best practices on issues related to land tenure security especially for women and vulnerable groups in customary jurisdictions; options/modalities for transparent, accountable and sustainable land-based management and investments; addressing land related conflicts; among others; enhancing capacity development for land governance etc; ii. Showcase information, communication and land administration technologies and innovations to enhance land governance and administration; iii. Provide a platform for networking among researchers, policy makers and other stakeholders with a view to improving the quality and quantity of research to address African specificities and emerging issues in land governance iv. Provide space for informed policy dialogue among stakeholders on policy options to enhance land governance, strengthen access to land by all land users and recognize the customary based land rights of African communities; and, v. Provide an opportunity for advocacy and resource mobilization in support of national and regional land policy initiatives geared towards enhanced land governance in Africa.

The overall objective of the Conference is to deepen commitment and strengthen capacity for land policy development, implementation and monitoring in Africa through improved access to knowledge and information in support of evidence-based land policy making.

- As planned the fifth edition of the Conference on Land Policy in Africa (CLPA) was successfully held from November 2024, 2023, hosted by the African Union Commission (AUC) in collaboration with the Government of Ethiopia. The theme for this edition was "Promoting Sustainable Land Governance in Africa for Accelerating Implementation of the AfCFTA."
-This edition featured 120 papers and had 1,043 registered participants, with 240 attending online. The CLPA facilitated the exchange and acquisition of new knowledge, linking academics, policymakers, and decision makers. It inspired participants from both the policy and development arenas to leverage their influence to shape the land governance landscape in Africa, particularly focusing on the nexus between land governance and the AfCFTA.
- A significant focus of this edition was the impact of land access on food production and, consequently, food surplus for intra Africa trade. It also provided a platform for sharing legal tools to resolve land based conflicts and address structural weaknesses in responsible agribusiness and investment in Africa, covering socioeconomic issues and development concerns on the continent.
- The Conference served as a robust platform for African leaders, scholars, and experts to exchange experiences, challenges, and successes concerning land reforms within their countries. This confluence fostered extensive dialogue, collaboration, and the mutual exchange of best practices and learned lessons. These interactions contributed to refining and enhancing future land reform policies and implementations across the continent.
- Additionally, the event was an opportunity to launch the African Unions Land Governance Strategy, marking a significant stride towards collaboration among African countries, the private sector, and development partners.
- The conference concluded with a call to action that highlighted key recommendations, demonstrating the important outcomes of the conference and its role as a convening platform for policy, advocacy, and lesson sharing. These recommendations are aimed at shaping and improving the implementation of the African Union Declaration on Land. This aligns with the successful implementation of the AfCFTA as a continent wide market for goods and services, business, and investment. This presents a major opportunity for African countries to boost growth, reduce poverty, and broaden economic inclusion and prosperity
